claims.quote: She was eight hundred feet long, of seventy thousand tons' displacement, seventy-five thousand horse-power, and on her trial trip had steamed at a rate of twenty-five knots an hour over the bottom
claims.description: An 800-foot, 70,000-ton, 75,000-horsepower passenger liner making 25 knots, far larger and faster than any ship then afloat.

claims.quote: From the bridge, engine-room, and a dozen places on her deck the ninety-two doors of nineteen water-tight compartments could be closed in half a minute by turning a lever.
claims.description: All the watertight doors of a giant liner can be closed within half a minute by a single lever from the bridge or other stations.

claims.quote: These doors would also close automatically in the presence of water.
claims.description: Watertight doors that close automatically when water enters a compartment.

claims.quote: With nine compartments flooded the ship would still float, and as no known accident of the sea could possibly fill this many
claims.description: A liner divided into compartments so that it is considered practically unsinkable.

claims.quote: Unsinkable—indestructible, she carried as few boats as would satisfy the laws.
claims.description: Because the ship is believed unsinkable it carries only the legal minimum of lifeboats, enough for a fraction of those aboard.

claims.quote: She would steam at full speed in fog, storm, and sunshine, and on the Northern Lane Route, winter and summer, for the following good and substantial reasons
claims.description: A steamship company openly adopts a policy of running its liner at full speed in fog and storm on the northern Atlantic route.

claims.quote: in case of an end-on collision with an iceberg—the only thing afloat that she could not conquer—her bows would be crushed in but a few feet further at full than at half speed
claims.description: The giant liner's one real danger is a collision with an iceberg on the North Atlantic route.
The giant liner Titan is wrecked.

claims.quote: Cold is negative heat, and can be treated like radiant energy, decreasing as the square of the distance.
claims.description: Locating icebergs in fog by measuring how fast the air temperature drops, treating cold as radiation that falls off with the square of distance.

claims.quote: that I may help to arouse such a sentiment of anger in the two countries as will forever end this wanton destruction of life and property for the sake of speed
claims.description: Public outrage in Britain and America ends the practice of liners running down smaller vessels for the sake of speed.
